evidenceAudit.scope: Adults considered for bariatric (metabolic) surgery: referral thresholds, expedited assessment for type 2 diabetes, multidisciplinary assessment, VTE and antibiotic prophylaxis. Verified against NICE NG246 (2025) and NG89; antibiotic prophylaxis from Saudi MOH Protocol-015 (gastroduodenal/bariatric). pathophysiology.summary: Bariatric surgery (e.g. sleeve gastrectomy, gastric bypass) produces large sustained weight loss and improves type 2 diabetes, hypertension, sleep apnoea and fatty liver. It requires lifelong follow-up for nutrition and complications.
keyMechanisms: Restriction and altered gut hormones reduce appetite and improve insulin sensitivity.
Bypass procedures cause malabsorption of iron, B12, calcium and vitamin D — lifelong supplements and monitoring.
Obesity and major abdominal surgery raise VTE risk (NICE NG89).

symptoms: Obesity with weight-related conditions: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, sleep apnoea, fatty liver, idiopathic intracranial hypertension.
redFlags: Uncontrolled psychiatric illness or eating disorder — address before surgery
Pregnancy planned within the post-operative period — discuss (NICE)

ruleIn.expectedFinding: BMI 40+, or 35–39.9 with a significant condition improved by weight loss; Middle Eastern background: 2.5 lower (NICE).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Refer for MDT assessment; person must agree to lifelong follow-up.

clinicalManagement.title: Referral
actions: Refer for full specialist assessment if BMI 40+ or 35–39.9 with a significant health condition, and the person agrees to long-term follow-up (NICE NG246 1.18.1).
Use thresholds 2.5 kg/m² lower for Middle Eastern background (NICE 1.18.2).
Expedited assessment for recent-onset type 2 diabetes with BMI 35+; consider at 30–34.9 (NICE 1.18.3–1.18.4).

clinicalManagement.title: MDT assessment
actions: Assess medical, nutritional and psychological needs, previous weight-management attempts, inequalities and fitness for anaesthesia; discuss benefits, risks, pregnancy plans and lifelong requirements (NICE 1.18.7–1.18.8).

clinicalManagement.title: Peri-operative
actions: VTE: mechanical prophylaxis from admission plus pharmacological prophylaxis (NICE NG89 1.14.5–1.14.6).
Antibiotics: cefazolin 2 g IV (3 g if 120 kg or more) within 60 min; allergy clindamycin 900 mg + ciprofloxacin 400 mg (MOH p. 1); stop within 24 h.
